result.reason: Both items — the Mishnah introducing the mekabel sadeh case and the Gemara defining makat medina — belong under 'Hamekabel Sadeh', whose prose explicitly introduces and explains this very Mishnah and its chakhirut lease framework, making it the primary home for this passage rather than 'Blight on Plain' which covers only the Gemara's definitional discussion.
Both items together constitute Ulla's chain of unresolved questions from the West (ba'u b'ma'arva) ending with teiku, which is precisely what candidate 1 ('Ulla's Questions') describes in its prose.

Both items — the question about planting barley instead of wheat and the Gemara's resolution citing 'v'tigzar omer v'yakum lach' — are precisely the content described in the 'Wrong Crop Case' prose, which explicitly discusses this scenario and quotes that very verse.

The passage describes the case where all the owner's fields were blighted and this field was also blighted but the majority of the valley was not — exactly matching the 'Owner's Fields Destroyed' section prose, which discusses this same scenario where the lessee argues the destruction stems from the owner's bad mazal.

All three items are continuous Gemara discussion about the case where all the tenant's fields and most of the valley were blighted, directly matching the 'All Fields Blighted' prose which describes this exact scenario including the 'remnant' argument from Jeremiah 42:2.

All three items together form the objection from Arakhin and its resolution — exactly what candidate 1 ('Blight Exclusions') describes: the mishna in Arakhin seems to limit makat medina to total crop failure, and the Gemara answers that the Arakhin rule is governed by the verse 'shenei tevuot' and is therefore not comparable to the lease-law rule in Bava Metzia.

The passage is precisely the exchange between Rav Ashi and Rav Kahana about why Shevi'it is excluded despite produce existing outside Eretz Yisrael, answered by 'afkata diMalka,' which is exactly what the 'Shevi'it Exception' prose describes.

The passage covers exactly the Hekdesh Paradox content: Mar Zutra's challenge about why Shevi'it counts in the hekdesh redemption calculation and Ravina's resolution about using the land for spreading produce, which is precisely what the prose under heading 0 describes.

The passage contains Shmuel's statement introducing the limitation on the mishnah's makat medina rule (lo shanu — only if planted and sprouted), which is precisely what candidate 1 'Shmuel's Caveat' describes, while candidate 2 'Divine Verse Argument' describes only the rationale/verse that follows, not the primary content of Shmuel's ruling itself.

All three items form a single continuous sugya about the shepherd/wolf/lion case, Rav Sheshet's objection, the miracle argument, and the unresolved 'kashya' — exactly what the 'Shepherd & Wolves' prose describes in detail.

Both items together present exactly the content described in candidate 1's prose: the contradiction between the two baraitot and its resolution via the machloket between Rabbi and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel over whether chazakah requires two or three occurrences — which is precisely what candidate 1's prose discusses in detail.

The passage contains both Reish Lakish's qualification (the main content) and Rav Pappa's answer about the end of the planting season as a single continuous Gemara unit, and Heading 0's prose explicitly discusses both elements together under 'Resh Lakish,' while Heading 1 treats Rav Pappa's answer as a separate discussion point — the passage belongs under Heading 0 where all its content is addressed as one unit.

All four items form the continuous baraita objection and its resolution (the six seasonal divisions, Rabbi Yehuda/Shimon's variations, and the charfei/aflei answer), which is precisely what the 'Seasonal Divisions' prose describes in full.
Both items describe the aspasta/barley case and Ravina's ruling that the land performed its owner's mission, which is precisely what candidate 0 ('Fodder to Barley') discusses in its prose.
Both items directly discuss the spoiled wine case and Rav Ashi's distinction about whether the land performed its mission, which is precisely what the 'Spoiled Wine' section's prose describes.

The mishnah covers both the barley/wheat rule and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's position as a single unified passage, and the prose under heading 0 explicitly describes all of this content including the RSbG prohibition, making it the better home for the complete mishnah.
